rationale: lpbench is a tiny (8 functions, ~5 KB text) numeric benchmark whose hot path is dominated by dense linear-algebra kernels (dgefa, dgesl, daxpy, matgen) and FFT loops, so the table favors cheap, low-risk data-level transforms (SUB, SPLIT get high Security/Diversity weights with minimal cost/risk weights) that apply broadly without perturbing inner-loop throughput, while heavier control-flow transforms are deliberately throttled: BCF and FLA carry high RuntimeCost/SizeCost (and FLA high CorrectnessRisk) weights so the selector limits them to the larger, less iteration-dense functions like main rather than the O(n^3)/O(n^2) kernels where loop-body bloat and dispatcher overhead would dominate; IBR and ICALL get moderate security weights but elevated runtime/correctness weights since indirect branches and calls in tight numeric loops degrade branch prediction and add few call sites to hide in this program; IGV is kept with modest security weight but a high SizeCost weight because globalization of locals inflates the already-compact binary and risks aliasing-related correctness issues in pointer-heavy LAPACK-style code, while still contributing diversity for static analyzers diffing across builds.
